Hi Sean / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed during procurement, Novamed needs a concise list of the operational evidence you can provide to demonstrate EU-only processing and controls related to Schrems II (SCCs). Specifically we need: 

- Confirmation that customer data (production + backups) is stored and processed only in EU regions (no cross-border backups)
- Details on KMS key ownership and where keys are stored
- Retention and deletion flow (how deletion requests are executed and certified)
- Any legal hold / compliance exceptions and how they are handled
- A copy of any SCC amendments or Data Processing Agreement (DPA) language relevant to restricted transfers

Can you also indicate whether you can provide an exportable deletion certificate for completed deletion requests and an operational playbook we can attach to our internal audit?

If helpful, I attached a simple data map of our expected flows (column heads: dataset, region, retention, notes). Would appreciate a response by COB Tuesday as our security review is on Wednesday morning.

Thanks,
Anna

Hi Anna — appreciate the clear ask and the data map. High level answers below, and I attached an initial evidence checklist for your audit team.

Quick summary (details + attachments below):
- EU-only storage/processing: production + snapshots and backups are pinned to EU regions. No cross-border backups by default; emergency failover policy is restricted and requires customer-approved runbook.
- KMS: customer keys can be customer-managed in EU KMS (BYOK) or Redwood-managed EU KMS; keys for EU-only plans are logically scoped to EU region.
- Retention/deletion: we support on-demand deletion + retention policies per dataset; we produce a signed deletion certificate for audit when requested.
- Legal hold: legal-hold flags prevent deletion; both the hold creation and removal are logged and auditable. We document exceptions in the playbook.
- SCCs/DPA: we can execute standard SCCs with our amendment; Marissa will share the current SCC amendment PDF for signature.

Action items for next steps:
1) Marissa will attach the SCC amendment draft and confirm signature pathway (DocuSign).
2) Ben will produce a short technical note describing backup topology and failover constraints.
3) I will schedule a 30-min call with your privacy team for Tuesday 14:00 CET to walk through the evidence pack.

Attachments: evidence-checklist.csv (operational evidence + expected artifact types)

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Anna / Sean / Ben — adding legal/compliance context and the SCCs amendment. Please see notes inline and attached signed-sccs-amendment.pdf (redline-ready).

Notes: 
- SCCs and Transfer Risk: Redwood executes the EU Commission standard contractual clauses and includes supplementary technical and contractual measures in Annex II. Our standard mitigations include: access controls, encryption-at-rest and in-transit, EU KMS options, region-bound admin controls, and transparent routing/logging.
- Backups & Restores: Backups for EU-only plans are retained in-region for both primary and disaster recovery pools. In emergency cross-border restore scenarios, transfers require documented customer authorization and a narrow runbook (we do not perform unilateral transfers).
- Deletion Certification: We produce a time-stamped, signed deletion certificate (PDF) containing request id, datasets affected, deletion scope, and verification hashes. We can automate generation for batch deletions.
- Evidence scope: Our checklist indicates artifact types (logs, DB snapshots, KMS key fingerprints, DocuSign-signed SCC amendment, deletion certificate). We cannot provide raw KMS key material, only key identifiers and audit logs showing usage.

Please confirm whether DocuSign is acceptable for the SCCs amendment and whether you need us to escalate to a legal exec to sign faster.

attachments: signed-sccs-amendment.pdf (PDF — SCC amendment draft)
